pr_title: ansible-galaxy - define multiple galaxy instances in ansible.cfg
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Add the ability to specify multiple galaxy servers in a configuration file for install. Also add a way to reference a server with authentication in the `requirements.yml`. I still am in the middle of manually testing a few scenarios but this should be enough to get people going.

Fixes https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/60316

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
ansible-galaxy

issue_context.title: ansible-galaxy collections install -r requirements.yml to support multiple servers
issue_context.body:
<!--- Verify first that your feature was not already discussed on GitHub -->
<!--- Complete *all* sections as described, this form is processed automatically -->

##### SUMMARY
Currently, a single api-server must be specified per `ansible-galaxy` invocation via `ansible-galaxy --server mygalaxy.myhost.com`. When processing a `requirements.yml` file where collections could come from multiple different servers, this is problematic.

I would like a way to specify multiple collection servers in a single invocation of `ansible-galaxy`. Preferably, somewhere in the `requirements.yml` file.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Idea

##### COMPONENT NAME
ansible-galaxy

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
<!--- Describe how the feature would be used, why it is needed and what it would solve -->
The meat of the design decision for this feature is deciding where to store the credentials and relating the credentials to the specific server.

A couple of potential implementation examples that would meet my needs:
```yaml
collections: 
  - name: ansible.tower 
    server: automation-hub.cloud.redhat.com 
    api_key: blahblahblah 
  - name: awx.awx 
    server: galaxy.ansible.com 
    api_key: blah2blah2 
```
Obviously don't love the above solution because it encourages putting creds in a file that will be source controlled.
  
OR 

```yaml
collections: 
  - name: awx.awx 
    server: galaxy.ansible.com 
  - name: ansible.tower 
    server: galaxy.mysite.com 
```
With a corresponding tempish auth/config file.

```  
#~/.ansible_galaxy 
[galaxy.ansible.com] 
server=galaxy.mysite.com
api_key=deadbeef 

[automation-hub.cloud.redhat.com] 
server=galaxy.ansible.com 
api_key=blahblah 
```
Note that the above example implies that only 1 auth entry is allowed per-unique-url. A server name could be added in `requirements.yml` to relax.

Also note that in the second example I would need a way to specify the `.ansible_galaxy` to use. The need for this stems from a multi-tenant environment.
<!--- HINT: You can also paste gist.github.com links for larger files -->

For the first pass at this, we're going to implement a list of servers specified in the galaxy config file. See the [comment in the ansible-galaxy source](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/cli/galaxy.py#L584). The idea is: attempt to download a collection from the list of servers according to some order of precedence, perhaps the order listed in the config file, top to bottom.

There's a comment in [this PR](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/59387#discussion_r305990492) from @jborean93 regarding the addition of multiple servers and tokens to the config file. He may already have plans for this work.
x2 check, but from code you can add server in `source` field of requirements, it won't work with auth though

@chrismeyersfsu I've just opened https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/60553 which allows you to define multiple Galaxy servers in the `ansible.cfg` file which are then used in the install process. From some basic tests it works fine but I am still need to do some more in depth testing tomorrow. Happy for you to give it a try and review the PR.
